miniProject.title: Expert-parallel MoE with balanced routing and honest accounting
miniProject.brief: Build the tiny MoE dispatcher in `parallel/` with packing, all-to-all exchange and combine, then balance, diagnose and cost it. Per-expert histograms, capacity math and placement records show where tokens move and which links pay.
steps: Implement the router and top-\(k\) selection in `parallel/` with deterministic ties, renormalized weights and shared-expert recombination, reporting token fractions and mean probabilities. Pass the Deep-ML sparse-expert and TensorTonic top-\(k\) router cases, then keep the hand derivation as the first regression.

Pack rows by expert and rank with a permutation in `parallel/`, exchange counts and payload over all-to-all with explicit splits, and invert the permutation on combine. Prove token identity and gradient flow against `model/` oracle with uneven and empty splits, confirmed by a Gloo run.

Build the rank-coordinate mapper for expert and expert-tensor groups in `comm/`, with round-trip and invalid-configuration tests. Tabulate one dense and sparse mesh composition with validation checks, keeping routed experts sparse and gate and shared state dense, plus one rejected configuration for each rule.

Derive per-expert capacity for one batch with drop and pad accounting, and show overflow behavior under skewed routing. Implement the auxiliary balancing loss and router z-loss with detached count fractions, passing the Deep-ML balancing-loss cases and contrasting bias routing without gradients.

Instrument per-expert histograms with drop counts and per-rank timing and communication splits in `trace/`, diagnosing one hotspot or empty-expert case. Harden the path with masked, repeated-token, router-gradient and empty-expert tests in the TorchTitan CPU style, using the Deep-ML routing cases as the recombination oracle.

Derive dispatch and combine bytes with memory accounting for one layer in `plan/`, state a placement with its contended links, and keep one measured-versus-predicted residual. Label CPU timings as accounting checks only, with link claims reserved for measured hardware.
deliverables: The `parallel/` dispatcher with packing, exchange, combine and routing oracles.
Group mapper, mesh tables, capacity math and imbalance evidence with one diagnosis.
`plan/` byte and memory accounting with placement, contended links and one residual.
`tests/` and `trace/` replaying identity, gradients and negative cases.

checks.name: Deep-ML 125 Sparse Mixture of Experts Layer
checks.note: Pass both forward tests; add routing and dispatch checks around them.

checks.name: TensorTonic Top-k MoE Router with Load Statistics
checks.note: Match order, dtype and device on all public cases exactly.

checks.name: Deep-ML 389 MoE Load Balancing Loss
checks.note: Derive both expected values from the formula before running.

checks.name: Deep-ML 229 Sparse MoE Top-K Routing
checks.note: Use as the recombination oracle beside masked and empty tests.

checks.name: TorchTitan CPU MoE unit tests
checks.note: Copy the padding, counter and transition patterns, not the framework.

rubric.pass: Uneven and empty splits round-trip token identity through a stable permutation, and gradients reach router and experts.
rubric.strong: A duplicated-token case and a swapped-split mutation each fail a named assertion.

rubric.pass: Coordinates round-trip, invalid configurations are rejected, and every family sits on its mesh.
rubric.strong: Each composition rule has a rejected configuration naming the exact rule broken.

rubric.pass: Capacity math predicts drops and pads, and balancing losses match expected values.
rubric.strong: Skewed routing shows where the buffer overflows, and bias routing is contrasted without gradients.

rubric.pass: Bytes count both exchanges, placement names contended links, and one residual is kept.
rubric.strong: CPU timings stay labeled as accounting checks, and the hotspot diagnosis names rank and expert.

miniProject.feedsInto: The dispatcher, histograms, mesh tables and byte accounting feed composed planning, fleet diagnosis and the capstone.
